00072 /**
00073  * @brief               Display an alert
00074  *
00075  * HxAlert displays a standard-sized alert, and returns after the user selects
00076  * a command button.  The button selected by the user is returned in the
00077  * pSelectedButton argument.
00078  *
00079  * The style argument represents which set of command buttons should be
00080  * displayed.
00081  *
00082  * pIcon is a 32 by 32 image that is drawn to the left of the alert message.
00083  * HxAlertGetIcon can be used to get the standard icons.  If pIcon is set to
00084  * NULL, no image is drawn.
00085  *
00086  * pTitle is drawn in the title bar of the alert.  If NULL is passed, the alert
00087  * has no title.
00088  *
00089  * pMessage is the body of the alert message.  The string is place in a static
00090  * field with no frame, to the right of the icon.  If the pMessage string does
00091  * not fit into the field, the system adds a frame and a scrollbar.  An error
00092  * is returned if this argument is NULL.
00093  * 
00094  * pSelectedButton in an input and output argument.  For input, it signifies
00095  * which command button has initial focus.  For output, it communicates which
00096  * command button was selected by the user.  The value of 0 represents the
00097  * leftmost command button ("OK" for kHxAlertStyleOKCancel or "Yes" for
00098  * kHxAlertStyleYesNo).  The value of 1 represents the second command button
00099  * ("Cancel" for kHxAlertStyleOKCancel or "No" for kHxAlertStyleYesNo).
00100  * If pSelectedButton is NULL, or if the input value of pSelectedButton is
00101  * more than (number of command buttons - 1), then the initial focus is given
00102  * to the leftmost command button.   The output value of pSelectedButton is
00103  * not defined if HxAlert does not return HX_OK.
00104  *
00105  * If you pass NULL for pSelectedButton, you're telling the API that
00106  * you want the first button selected and that you don't care about
00107  * what button was picked.  This is often used with informational
00108  * alerts that only have one button.
00109  *
00110  * The rightmost command button is used as the escape button (i.e., pressing
00111  * the tilde key calling HxDialogCloseAllDialogs acts on this button).
00112  *
00113  * @param id            IN:     Alert ID, or kHxWidgetAutoID to auto-generate
00114  *                              the ID
00115  * @param style         IN:     Command button style
00116  * @param pIcon         IN:     Pointer to icon, or NULL
00117  * @param pTitle        IN:     Title of alert, or NULL
00118  * @param pMessage      IN:     String for body of alert message
00119  * @param pSelectedButton  IN/OUT: Pointer to number of selected command button
00120  *                              or NULL if information not needed.  
00121  *                              The value pointed to by pSelectedButton will be
00122  *                              used to pick the button that has initial focus.
00123  *
00124  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.  Returns
00125  *                              HX_INVALID_ARG if style is not valid, or if
00126  *                              pMessage is NULL.
00127  *
00128  **/
00129 HxResult HxAlert(uint32_t id, HxAlertButtonStyle_t style,
00130                     HxImageDescription_t* pIcon,
00131                     const char* pTitle, const char* pMessage,
00132                     uint32_t* pSelectedButton);
00133 
00134 /**
00135  * @brief               Display a custom alert
00136  *
00137  * HxAlert displays a custom alert, and returns after the user selects a
00138  * command button.
00139  *
00140  * If pBounds is NULL, the alert is centered in the display, and the width
00141  * and height are set to kHxAlertDefaultWidth and kHxAlertDefaultHeight.
00142  *
00143  * This function allows the application to customize the size of the alert
00144  * window, and the command button set.  At least one command button label
00145  * must be defined.
00146  *
00147  * pSelectedButton in an input and output argument.  For input, it
00148  * signifies which command button has initial focus.  For output, it
00149  * communicates which command button was selected by the user.  The
00150  * value of 0 represents the leftmost command button, 1 the second
00151  * button, and 2 the third one.  If pSelectedButton is NULL, or if the
00152  * input value of pSelectedButton is more than (number of command
00153  * buttons - 1), then the initial focus is given to the leftmost
00154  * command button.  The output value of pSelectedButton is not defined
00155  * if HxAlertCustom does not return HX_OK.
00156  *
00157  * If you pass NULL for pSelectedButton, you're telling the API that
00158  * you want the first button selected and that you don't care about
00159  * what button was picked.  This is often used with informational
00160  * alerts that only have one button.
00161  *
00162  * The rightmost command button is used as the escape button (i.e., pressing
00163  * the tilde key calling HxDialogCloseAllDialogs acts on this button).
00164  *
00165  * @param id            IN:     Alert ID
00166  * @param pBounds       IN:     Bounds of the dialog, or NULL
00167  * @param pIcon         IN:     Pointer to icon, or NULL
00168  * @param pTitle        IN:     Title of alert, or NULL
00169  * @param pMessage      IN:     String for body of alert message
00170  * @param pButtonLabel1 IN:     String for first command button
00171  * @param pButtonLabel2 IN:     String for second command button, or NULL
00172  * @param pButtonLabel3 IN:     String for third command button, or NULL
00173  * @param pSelectedButton  IN/OUT: Pointer to number of selected command button
00174  *                              or NULL if information not needed.  
00175  *                              The value pointed to by pSelectedButton will be
00176  *                              used to pick the button that has initial focus.
00177  *
00178  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.  Returns
00179  *                              HX_INVALID_ARG if pButtonLabel1 or pMessage
00180  *                              are NULL.
00181  *
00182  **/
00183 HxResult HxAlertCustom(uint32_t id, const HxRectangle_t* pBounds,
00184                     HxImageDescription_t* pIcon, const char* pTitle,
00185                     const char* pMessage, const char* pButtonLabel1,
00186                     const char* pButtonLabel2, const char* pButtonLabel3,
00187                     uint32_t* pSelectedButton);

00189 /**

00194  * to kHxAlertNoButtonSelected.
00195  *
00196  * @param selector      IN:     The ID of the alert to dismiss.  If the ID
00197  *                              does not match the topmost alert's id,
00198  *                              nothing happens.
00199  *
00200  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.
00201  *
00202  **/
00203 HxResult HxAlertDismiss(uint32_t id);
